text: A glass pane, a Copper Resonator and a Spirit Shard make a lens for ley sight. Look through it and you see what the land and your camp are doing: how strong the ley is, where Pulse reaches, which totems are awake and which machines are working.

pages.title: Four sights
text: Hold it in either hand and use it to cycle through four sights:
- **Ley**: paints the ground in a **17 by 17** square, blue where the land is quiet and gold where it sings.
- **Pulse zone**: marks blocks that hold Pulse, and the **8-block** ring they can reach.
- **Voices**: tints nearby totems gold when answered, dull when dim, grey when quiet.
- **Machines**: marks the Tribal Power machines around you.
While you hold it, a line on your screen shows the ley strength where you stand.

pages.title: Reading the ground
pages.text: Gold is where a Ley Collector would sing loudest; blue is where it would barely hum.

pages.title: Up close
text: Sneak-use the lens on a Ley Collector to print that collector's exact factor breakdown in chat: the same numbers it collects with.
Sneak-use it on a lattice animal or remnant to print its threads and Marks. The charm does not change those rolls.

The ley sight counts the same things the collector does, for a beat from 1 to **16**. A beat of **8 or more** keeps nearby totems awake; the Pulse stored in a collector does not. A roof takes away sky, rain and storm, but water, plants, voices, a hearth and animals still add.
